nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A structured troubleshooting process beats random guessing every time. The classic flow: identify the problem precisely, form a theory, test it, fix, verify, document. Most exams test that you know the flow AND can spot the layer at which the symptom originates.

flashcards.back: CompTIA's 6-step: (1) Identify the problem (gather symptoms, questions to user, recent changes). (2) Establish a theory of probable cause. (3) Test the theory. (4) Plan and implement the fix. (5) Verify full system functionality, apply preventive measures. (6) Document everything.

flashcards.front: Top-down vs bottom-up troubleshooting on a network problem.
flashcards.back: Top-down: start at the application layer and work down — does the browser work? DNS? TCP? Routing? Bottom-up: start at the physical layer — is the cable plugged in? Link light? IP? When you suspect physical/cable, bottom-up is faster. When the user has 'a website is broken', top-down is faster.

Almost every production incident traces back to a recent change — a deploy, a config push, a vendor patch, a cert rotation. 'It was working yesterday' tells you to check today's change-log before forming an exotic theory. Recent changes are the highest-priors of the bug space.

Bisect the path between symptom and cause. If 10 hops between client and server, test hop 5. Good → problem is past hop 5. Bad → problem is before. Two more bisections narrow it to one hop. Faster than checking every link sequentially when the chain is long.

questions.q: An administrator must prevent all users on the internal network from accessing social media sites during business hours (08:00–17:00, Mon–Fri) but allow access outside these hours. What combination of FortiGate features achieves this?
choices: Configure IP-based ACLs blocking known social media IP ranges using FortiGuard IP reputation feeds
Create an application control profile blocking social media categories and attach it to a permanent security policy
Configure a web filter profile with social media categories set to Block;.
Enable DNS filtering to block social media categories in the DNS security policy without time restrictions
questions.explanation: FortiGate web filter profiles support category-based blocking (social media includes Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, etc.). A schedule object defines when the blocking policy is active. The two-policy pattern: (1) Policy with schedule + blocking web filter = blocks during business hours; (2) Policy without schedule + permissive web filter = allows at all times, but only matches after policy 1 expires. Application control (option A) cannot apply time-based schedules as precisely. attach it to a security policy with a recurring schedule object (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00); a second policy with no schedule allows access outside business hours

questions.q: A user reports they cannot access a specific website. The FortiGate web filter log shows the site is blocked under the 'Unrated' category. The administrator verifies the site is legitimate. What is the quickest solution?
choices: Override the site's rating by adding its URL to a web filter URL override list with an 'Allow' action
Create a custom URL category containing the site's URL and configure the web filter profile to allow that custom category
Submit the site to FortiGuard for re-categorization and wait for the rating database to update
Disable the 'Unrated' category blocking in the web filter profile to allow all unrated sites
questions.explanation: The quickest operational solution is to add the site's URL to a web filter URL override (allow list) in the web filter profile. URL overrides take precedence over category-based rules. The override can be applied immediately. Submitting for re-categorization (option B) is correct long-term but may take days. Disabling Unrated (option C) is a security risk.

questions.q: A FortiGate security policy uses proxy-based inspection with a web filter profile. An administrator notices that some web traffic bypasses the web filter checks. After investigation, they find the traffic uses HTTPS on port 8443. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The FortiGate requires a separate policy for non-standard HTTPS ports with the same web filter profile applied

The web filter profile only inspects traffic on the standard HTTPS port (443); traffic on port 8443 must be included in the SSL inspection profile's port range so the FortiGate can decrypt and inspect it

The proxy-based security profile only processes traffic identified by the FortiGate as HTTP/HTTPS based on the protocol type in the service object — the security policy must include a service object covering TCP/8443
Port 8443 requires a custom application signature in Application Control before the FortiGate web filtering engine can apply inspection to that port
questions.explanation: The FortiGate policy service object must include the port used by the traffic. If the security policy's service is 'HTTPS' (which only covers port 443), traffic on port 8443 won't match that policy. Create a service object for HTTPS-ALT (port 8443) and include it in the policy. Also ensure the SSL/SSH inspection profile includes port 8443 for deep inspection.

questions.q: A FortiGate administrator wants to configure web filtering to allow access to the 'Video Streaming' category only for the marketing department users, while blocking it for all other users. What is the correct approach?
choices: Configure a single web filter profile with 'Video Streaming' set to Allow and apply it to all users; use application control to restrict video by user group
Create two security policies: one for marketing users (linked via FSSO group) with a permissive web filter profile.
Configure web filter URL overrides for all video streaming sites and assign them to the marketing LDAP group
Enable user authentication in the web filter profile and configure per-user URL exceptions for marketing accounts
questions.explanation: The standard FortiGate approach for group-based web filtering: create two policies ordered top-to-bottom. Policy 1: source = marketing group (authenticated via FSSO or explicit auth), web filter profile = allows video. Policy 2: source = all, web filter profile = blocks video. Because policies are evaluated top-down first-match, marketing users match policy 1; everyone else falls through to policy 2. and one for all other users with a restrictive profile — place the marketing policy above in the policy list

questions.q: A FortiGate web filter profile is configured to redirect blocked websites to a FortiGate-hosted 'Access Denied' page. Users report the block page is not appearing — instead they see a browser connection error. What is the most likely cause?
choices: SSL deep inspection is not enabled.
The block page only displays when the security policy uses proxy-based inspection mode; flow-based mode cannot deliver block pages
The FortiGate's interface must have HTTPS management access enabled to serve block pages to clients
The FortiGuard web filtering license has expired, preventing block page delivery for category-blocked sites
questions.explanation: For HTTPS sites blocked by web filter, FortiGate cannot return an HTML block page without SSL deep inspection. Without decryption, the FortiGate resets the TLS connection, causing browsers to show 'ERR_CONNECTION_RESET' or a certificate error — not a readable block page. Enable SSL deep inspection (full certificate inspection mode) and ensure the FortiGate CA certificate is trusted by client browsers to display the HTML block page for HTTPS sites. for HTTPS blocked sites, FortiGate must terminate the TLS session to return an HTML block page; without SSL inspection, the browser receives a TLS connection error instead of the block page

nodes.title: High availability: Key Ideas
nodes.content: HA means designing so a single failure doesn't take the service down. Build redundancy at every layer the SLA cares about — power, network, compute, storage, region. Measure with availability percentages (the 9s) and recovery objectives (RTO/RPO).

flashcards.front: Active-active vs active-passive — when do you use each?
flashcards.back: Active-active: both nodes serve traffic; failure of one cuts capacity in half but service continues — no failover delay. Active-passive: only primary serves traffic; secondary is hot standby, takes over on failure with seconds-to-minutes delay. Active-active is harder (concurrency, conflict resolution) but better RTO. Active-passive is simpler — pick it for stateful systems that can't easily multi-write (most RDBMS).

flashcards.front: RTO vs RPO — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: RTO (Recovery Time Objective): how long until the service is back. RPO (Recovery Point Objective): how much data you can afford to lose. An RTO of 4h + RPO of 15 min means 'we can be down 4 hours and lose up to the last 15 minutes of writes'. Drives architecture choices: tight RPO needs synchronous replication; loose RPO allows async backups.

flashcards.front: The 'nines' — what does 99.9% vs 99.99% mean in real time?
flashcards.back: 99% (two 9s): ~3.65 days/yr of downtime. 99.9% (three 9s): ~8.76 hours/yr. 99.99%: ~52 minutes/yr. 99.999% (five 9s): ~5 minutes/yr. Each 9 typically multiplies cost ~10x because you need geographic redundancy, faster failover, and a much smaller deploy blast radius. Don't promise more 9s than the business actually values.

flashcards.front: Why is testing failover the hardest part of HA?
flashcards.back: An HA setup that's never been tested isn't HA — it's hope. Real-world failure modes are messier than 'kill primary' tests: cert expiry, DNS TTLs, partial-write states, split brain, runbooks out of date. Chaos engineering (Netflix's Chaos Monkey, AWS Fault Injection Simulator) makes failure normal — small failures every week so the big one isn't novel.

questions.q: An administrator must ensure a FortiGate high-availability (HA) active-passive cluster maintains session continuity so that existing TCP sessions are not dropped during a failover. Which HA feature must be enabled?
choices: Enable heartbeat interfaces on both FortiGate units to detect when the primary goes down — heartbeat detects failure but does not replicate active sessions from the primary to the secondary
Enable session synchronization in the HA configuration to replicate active sessions from primary to secondary
Configure gratuitous ARP on the cluster's interface to update network switches about the MAC address change — this handles Layer 2 convergence but does not preserve active session state
Configure the HA virtual MAC address to ensure transparent failover without ARP cache issues — this prevents MAC flapping but does not synchronize active session entries to the secondary
questions.explanation: Session synchronization (session pickup) in HA: the primary FortiGate continuously replicates session table entries to the secondary. When failover occurs, the secondary already has the session state and can continue existing connections without dropping them. Without session sync, all sessions must be re-established after failover.

questions.q: A company deploys FortiGate in active-active HA mode. The administrator notices that the secondary unit is not processing any traffic despite being healthy. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The secondary unit requires a separate FortiGate license to process traffic in active-active mode
Load-balancing configuration is not set correctly.
Active-active HA only activates the secondary unit when the primary fails, similar to active-passive
The secondary unit's interfaces are not connected to the same network switch as the primary
questions.explanation: In active-active HA, both units process traffic simultaneously. The primary unit receives all traffic and load-balances sessions to both itself and the secondary based on the configured method (by source/destination IP, etc.). If the secondary is not processing traffic, check the HA load-balancing schedule and ensure the primary is properly distributing sessions. in active-active mode the primary load-balances sessions to secondary based on the HA load-balancing method

questions.q: FortiGate is configured with an active-passive HA cluster. After a power failure on the primary, the secondary unit takes over. When the primary comes back online, what happens by default?
choices: The secondary continues as the active unit; the primary remains as standby until manually failed back over
The primary immediately reclaims the active role and the secondary returns to standby
Both units enter a negotiation state and the unit with the higher serial number becomes active
The administrator must manually trigger a failback using the CLI command 'execute ha manage' on the recovered
questions.explanation: In FortiGate HA, when override is disabled (default), the secondary keeps the active role after recovering from a primary failure — there is no automatic preemption. The recovered unit becomes the standby. If override is enabled, the highest-priority unit can automatically reclaim active status. Most production deployments disable override to minimize disruption.

questions.q: An organization uses FortiGate in active-passive HA. The HA heartbeat interfaces are configured but the secondary unit shows 'unmanaged' status. What should the administrator verify?
choices: Verify the heartbeat cable connects the dedicated HA interfaces directly between the two FortiGate units

Ensure the management interfaces on both FortiGate units have valid IPs — the management interface is used for out-of-band access but is not required for HA heartbeat communication between the two FortiGate interfaces
Check that both FortiGate units have matching HA group name and password — FortiGate units pair by group name, not by serial number
Verify both FortiGate units are running identical FortiOS firmware versions with matched interface configurations — a firmware mismatch can prevent HA formation
questions.explanation: FortiGate HA heartbeat must be connected via the dedicated heartbeat interfaces (directly cabled or via a switch). Both units must have matching HA group name and password in the HA configuration. If these don't match, units cannot form a cluster. Also verify both units run the same FortiOS firmware version. A management IP mismatch won't prevent HA formation — the heartbeat interface handles it.

nodes.title: VPN and secure connectivity: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A VPN tunnels private traffic over the public internet, encrypting it end-to-end. Site-to-site VPNs connect networks (e.g., on-prem to cloud); client VPNs connect individual devices to a private network. Both rely on IPsec or SSL/TLS.

flashcards.front: Site-to-site VPN vs client VPN — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: Site-to-site VPN connects two networks (typical: on-prem data center ↔ cloud VPC) using gateway devices on each side. Client VPN connects an individual user's laptop to a private network for remote access. Site-to-site uses IPsec, client VPN often uses SSL or WireGuard.

Phase 1 (IKE) authenticates the two peers (pre-shared key or certificate) and builds a secure management channel. Phase 2 negotiates the actual data tunnel (encryption algorithm, key lifetime). Most exam questions test that phase 1 must succeed before phase 2.

flashcards.front: When do you pick a dedicated link over a VPN?
flashcards.back: VPN over the public internet is cheap but variable — bandwidth and latency depend on internet weather. Dedicated links (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect) are private fiber with consistent latency and bandwidth — pick them for production traffic that must be predictable, or compliance scenarios that forbid the public internet.

flashcards.front: What's the BGP tunnel option for?
flashcards.back: VPNs can use static routes or BGP. BGP-based VPNs auto-propagate route changes between sides (add a new subnet on-prem → cloud learns it within seconds). Static VPN requires manual route updates every time the topology changes. Always pick BGP for production.

questions.q: An administrator needs to configure a site-to-site IPsec VPN between a FortiGate (HQ) and a branch office FortiGate. Both have static public IPs. The tunnel must use IKEv2 with pre-shared key authentication. Which Phase 1 settings are mandatory?
choices: Remote gateway IP, pre-shared key, and Phase 2 selectors included in the Phase 1 configuration
ISAKMP port (UDP 500), remote gateway IP, and NAT-T enabled to handle NAT traversal between sites
Remote gateway IP, pre-shared key, and IKE version set to 2;.
Remote gateway IP, digital certificate, and Diffie-Hellman group; certificates are required for IKEv2
questions.explanation: IPsec Phase 1 (IKE SA) negotiates the secure channel for key exchange. Mandatory settings: remote peer IP (or hostname), authentication method (PSK or certificate — PSK means pre-shared key), IKE version (2 for IKEv2), and encryption/authentication proposals. Phase 1 does NOT include Phase 2 selectors — those are defined in Phase 2 (IPsec SA). Certificates are an alternative to PSK, not required for IKEv2. Phase 1 negotiates the IKE SA (encryption and authentication algorithms)

questions.q: An administrator configures a site-to-site IPsec VPN tunnel between two FortiGates. Phase 1 completes successfully but Phase 2 never establishes. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The pre-shared key is different on both sides of the tunnel
IKE proposals in Phase 1 are incompatible between the two FortiGate devices
The Phase 2 tunnel (quick mode) selectors define the traffic to encrypt.
The HA configuration on one FortiGate is preventing Phase 2 from completing while Phase 1 is on the standby unit
questions.explanation: IPsec Phase 2 defines the traffic selectors (what source/destination subnets are encrypted in the tunnel). The selectors must match exactly on both sides. If HQ defines the tunnel as 10.1.0.0/24 ↔ 10.2.0.0/24 but the branch defines it as 10.1.0.0/16 ↔ 10.2.0.0/16, the Quick Mode negotiation fails. Pre-shared key mismatch (option A) would cause Phase 1 to fail. if the source/destination subnet configurations do not match exactly on both ends, Phase 2 fails to negotiate

questions.q: A FortiGate is receiving IPsec VPN connections from remote FortiClients but some clients with dynamic IP addresses cannot establish the VPN. The Phase 1 is configured with the remote gateway set to a static IP. What change resolves this?
choices: Change the remote gateway type in Phase 1 from 'Static IP Address' to 'Dialup User' to accept connections
Switch from IKEv1 to IKEv2 — IKEv2 improves re-keying and supports multiple connections but still requires the remote gateway to be set to accept connections from dynamic IPs
Enable NAT-T (NAT Traversal) on the Phase 1 gateway configuration to support clients behind NAT — NAT-T handles UDP encapsulation but does not change how the gateway handles dynamic source IPs
Configure a separate Phase 1 for each possible client IP address as static entries — this requires knowing all client IPs in advance and cannot accept connections from truly dynamic addresses
questions.explanation: For remote access VPN (FortiClient connecting to FortiGate), configure the Phase 1 remote gateway type as 'Dialup User'. This tells the FortiGate to accept IKE connections from any source IP. The FortiGate becomes the VPN server and clients can connect from any IP. Aggressive mode with dial-up is the standard FortiGate remote access VPN pattern.

questions.q: FortiGate has an IPsec VPN tunnel that has been working correctly. Users report they can no longer access resources across the tunnel. What is the first CLI diagnostic command the administrator should run to verify the tunnel status?
choices: diagnose vpn ike status — displays IKE SA status and tunnel negotiation information
get vpn ipsec tunnel summary.
get vpn ipsec stats tunnel — shows packet counters and errors for all IPsec tunnels
diagnose debug application ike -1 — enables verbose IKE debugging to trace tunnel negotiation in real time
questions.explanation: 'get vpn ipsec tunnel summary' provides a quick overview of all IPsec tunnels: Phase 1 status (up/down), Phase 2 selectors (active/inactive), bytes in/out, and uptime. This is the first check to determine if the tunnel is up or down. If the tunnel is down, use 'diagnose vpn ike status' or debug flow for deeper investigation. shows Phase 1 and Phase 2 status, up/down state, and traffic statistics for all IPsec tunnels

nodes.title: Mixed exam topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Some exam objectives don't fit neatly into a single domain — they span protocols, tools, or concepts covered briefly in multiple sections. These cards treat each item as a stand-alone fact, the way an exam question presents it: one concept, one answer.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a hub, a switch, and a router?
flashcards.back: Hub: Layer 1, repeats every frame to all ports — all devices share bandwidth, collisions guaranteed. Switch: Layer 2, forwards frames using a MAC address table to only the destination port — full duplex, no collisions, each port gets full bandwidth. Router: Layer 3, makes forwarding decisions based on IP address, connects different networks. Hub is legacy; switches dominate LAN; routers are at network edges.

flashcards.front: What is RAID 5 and how many drives can it tolerate losing?
flashcards.back: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across at least 3 drives. Any single drive failure can be recovered by reconstructing missing data from the remaining drives and parity. It cannot tolerate 2 simultaneous drive failures. Effective capacity = (N-1) × drive size. Read performance is excellent; write requires parity recalculation. RAID 6 tolerates 2 failures using double parity.

flashcards.front: What does a proxy server do, and how does a forward proxy differ from a reverse proxy?
flashcards.back: Forward proxy: sits between clients and the internet on behalf of clients — used for content filtering, caching, and anonymizing outbound requests (the server sees the proxy's IP). Reverse proxy: sits in front of servers on behalf of the server — used for load balancing, SSL termination, caching, and hiding backend topology (the client sees the proxy's IP). Both intermediate HTTP, but they protect opposite sides.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network architecture?
flashcards.back: A demilitarized zone is a network segment between the untrusted internet and the trusted internal network, typically protected by two firewalls (or two interfaces on one firewall). Public-facing services (web, email, DNS) sit in the DMZ: internet can reach them but not the internal network; if the DMZ host is compromised, the inner firewall still blocks access to the internal LAN.

questions.q: An administrator needs to allow external users on the internet to access an internal web server (192.168.1.100) on port 80 via the FortiGate's WAN IP (203.0.113.10). Which FortiGate NAT feature should be configured?
choices: Central SNAT policy with the internal server's IP and the WAN interface as the source — this performs source NAT for outbound traffic, not inbound external access
Virtual IP (VIP) with mapped IP 192.168.1.100 and external IP 203.0.113.10.
Policy-based DNAT using the external WAN IP as the original destination and the server IP as the translated destination — FortiGate does not have a standalone DNAT policy object separate from VIPs
IP Pool with overload NAT to map outbound internal addresses to the external WAN IP — this is for source NAT, not for allowing external inbound connections
questions.explanation: Virtual IPs (VIPs) perform Destination NAT (DNAT) on FortiGate. Configure a VIP with External IP = 203.0.113.10 (WAN), Mapped IP = 192.168.1.100 (server). Create a security policy from WAN→LAN with the VIP as the destination. FortiGate translates the destination address before applying routing. Port forwarding is also configured in the VIP object. then reference the VIP as the destination in a security policy

questions.q: A FortiGate administrator wants to ensure that outgoing traffic from the LAN network (192.168.1.0/24) appears to come from the FortiGate's WAN IP address (203.0.113.10) when leaving the network. What NAT configuration achieves this?
choices: Create a central SNAT policy mapping source 192.168.1.0/24 to the WAN IP for outbound connections
Configure a Virtual IP with the WAN IP as the external address and the LAN subnet as the mapped range
Configure an IP Pool of type overload with 203.0.113.10 and attach it to the security policy via NAT
Enable NAT on the security policy for LAN-to-WAN traffic, which uses the outgoing interface's IP for SNAT
questions.explanation: Both options B and D achieve SNAT, but Central SNAT policy is the dedicated NAT configuration method in FortiOS. Central SNAT maps source addresses to a translated IP for outbound traffic. It keeps NAT logic separate from security policy. Enabling NAT on the policy (option B) also works but uses the outgoing interface's IP automatically — a Central SNAT policy provides more explicit control.

questions.q: A FortiGate security policy allows traffic from LAN to WAN but users cannot reach any websites. The FortiGate has a valid default route. Running 'diagnose debug flow' shows the traffic is accepted by the policy. What should the administrator check next?
choices: Check the FortiGuard subscription status — expired subscriptions can affect security profile features but do not block all web traffic accepted by a security policy
Verify that the security policy has NAT enabled or a Central SNAT policy exists to translate source addresses

Check that a NAT policy exists to translate internal addresses to the WAN IP before traffic leaves — without source NAT the security policy accepts traffic but the internet cannot route replies back to private addresses
Verify DNS resolution is working — check if FortiGate has a DNS server configured and users can resolve hostnames correctly
questions.explanation: If traffic is accepted by the security policy but still not reaching the internet, the most common cause is missing NAT. Without NAT (SNAT), the FortiGate forwards packets with the private source IP, which is not routable on the internet. Enable NAT on the policy (which uses the outgoing interface IP) or configure a Central SNAT policy. DNS (option A) would cause name resolution failures, not all web access failures.

questions.q: A FortiGate administrator needs to collect and correlate logs from multiple FortiGate devices across several branch offices into a single management console for analysis and reporting. Which Fortinet product is designed for this purpose?
choices: FortiAnalyzer, which collects logs.
FortiCloud, which provides a cloud-based dashboard for viewing real-time FortiGate status
FortiManager, which provides centralized policy management across multiple FortiGate devices — manages configuration, not logs collection and forensic analysis
FortiSIEM, which correlates logs from multiple vendors including FortiGate — broader than FortiAnalyzer and not the primary Fortinet-native logs collection platform for this use case
questions.explanation: FortiAnalyzer is Fortinet's centralized log and analytics platform. It receives syslog from multiple FortiGate devices, stores logs long-term, provides pre-built reports, event correlation, threat analytics, and compliance reporting. FortiManager handles centralized policy management (pushing configs); FortiAnalyzer handles log collection and analysis. Both are often deployed together. events, and traffic data from FortiGate devices and provides centralized reporting, correlation, and long-term log storage

questions.q: A FortiGate is receiving syslog events but the FortiAnalyzer shows no received logs. The FortiGate confirms logs are sent to the FortiAnalyzer IP. What should be checked on FortiAnalyzer?
choices: Ensure the FortiGate is registered/authorized in FortiAnalyzer under Device Manager.
Verify the FortiAnalyzer license includes the correct number of daily log gigabytes for the connected FortiGate
Check that the FortiAnalyzer syslog daemon is running and listening on UDP 514
Verify the FortiAnalyzer Fabric connector is enabled in FortiGate to push logs via the Fabric protocol
questions.explanation: FortiAnalyzer uses device authorization: only FortiGates that are registered and authorized in the FortiAnalyzer Device Manager can send logs. When a FortiGate connects for the first time, an authorization request appears in FortiAnalyzer; the admin must authorize it. Unauthorized devices' logs are silently dropped. This is a common gotcha when adding a new FortiGate to FortiAnalyzer. FortiAnalyzer only accepts logs from authorized devices

questions.q: A FortiGate is forwarding logs to a FortiAnalyzer. The organization requires that FortiGate logs be retained for 1 year for compliance. FortiAnalyzer's default retention is 30 days. What must be configured on FortiAnalyzer?
choices: Configure log archiving to move logs from the analytics tier to the archive tier with a 365-day retention policy.
Purchase additional FortiAnalyzer storage licenses and enable extended retention mode — adding storage expands capacity but does not by itself configure the logs retention period to 365 days
Increase the FortiAnalyzer analytics logs retention period to 365 days in the system settings — keeping all logs in the analytics tier for 365 days consumes far more disk than using the archive tier
Enable logs forwarding from FortiAnalyzer to a secondary FortiAnalyzer to extend total retention capacity — forwarding copies logs but does not configure the retention policy on either unit
questions.explanation: FortiAnalyzer has two tiers: analytics tier (recent data, hot storage for fast queries) and archive tier (compressed, cheaper storage for long-term retention). Configure the data policy with archive retention of 365 days. Archived logs are compressed and stored long-term; they can be retrieved for analysis when needed. Simply adjusting the analytics retention to 365 days is costly in disk space. ensuring logs are preserved for the compliance period

questions.q: A FortiGate IPS profile is set to Block for a known exploit signature. During testing, the FortiGate logs the IPS match but does not block the traffic. What should the administrator verify first?
choices: Verify the FortiGuard IPS subscription is active and signatures are up to date — an expired subscription prevents new pattern downloads but does not explain logging without blocking
Ensure the FortiGate SSL inspection certificate is installed in the client browsers
Check that the security policy uses proxy-based inspection mode instead of flow-based — without the correct inspection mode the FortiGate cannot enforce the IPS profile action
Confirm the IPS profile is configured with the signature action set to Block and not Monitor — if set to Monitor the FortiGate logs the match but does not block
questions.explanation: When FortiGate logs an IPS match but doesn't block, first ensure the SSL inspection profile covers the traffic (if HTTPS). For clear-text traffic, the most common oversight is that the security policy lacks a correctly configured inspection mode. Proxy-based mode provides full IPS capabilities. Also confirm the IPS sensor is attached to the correct policy and that the specific signature action within the sensor is set to Block, not Monitor.

questions.q: A FortiGate IPS sensor has a signature with a default action of 'Pass'. The administrator changes the action to 'Block' for this specific signature. After saving, traffic matching that signature continues to pass. What should be checked?
choices: Confirm the FortiGuard IPS subscription is renewed since expired subscriptions prevent signature action changes
Check that the IPS sensor is attached to the correct security policy, and that the policy has a valid inspection mode (flow or proxy)
Verify the FortiGate has sufficient memory to load the updated IPS signature database
The signature may have a filter override at a higher priority in the IPS sensor.
questions.explanation: IPS sensors can have both category-level filter overrides and individual signature overrides. If a filter entry (by category, severity, OS, etc.) matches the signature and is set to 'Pass' at a higher priority than the individual signature entry, the filter override wins. Check all filter entries in the IPS sensor to ensure no higher-priority filter is overriding the individual signature action. check filter-level overrides that may be set to Pass for that signature's category

finalBoss.title: Final Exam: Fortinet NSE 4 Network Security Professional
